_meta.description: Catalog of every live DAT_<hex-address> global symbol in the decompiled Ultima Underworld source tree (src/*.c, src/headers/*.h) -- i.e. every Ghidra address-named global still referenced somewhere in real code, not just mentioned in a historical comment.
_meta.generated_by: a one-off scripted pass (regex-based declaration/comment extraction + a full-codebase reader/writer occurrence scan), with rename_suggestion hand-reviewed per entry rather than pattern-matched -- free-text comment mining for names proved unreliable (it kept latching onto unrelated function/local names cited for context) and was discarded.

fields.name: the DAT_ symbol as it appears in source
fields.lives_in: the .c file (or header, if never given real .c storage) that owns its actual storage -- for a #define alias into a named backing array, this is the backing array's own owning file, not wherever the alias macro text happens to sit
fields.kind: scalar | array | macro_alias (an alias is still backed by real storage somewhere; this just says the DAT_ name itself is a #define, not the storage declaration)
fields.type: the C type of the actual storage (the backing array's element type for an alias, or the scalar/array's own declared type)
fields.backing_array: the real array symbol this name is an alias into, if any (null for a plain scalar or for an array declared directly under this same name)
fields.size: declared element count of the backing array, if this variable is backed by one; null for a plain scalar
fields.readers: count of source lines across src/*.c where this name is read (a regex heuristic: anything not immediately followed by an assignment/increment operator counts as a read; address-taken uses passed to another function are counted as reads, which undercounts writes that happen through a pointer)
fields.writers: count of source lines across src/*.c classified as a write by the same heuristic (=, +=, -=, *=, /=, &=, |=, ^=, <<=, >>=, ++, --)
fields.reader_file_count: number of distinct .c files containing at least one read occurrence
fields.writer_file_count: number of distinct .c files containing at least one write occurrence
fields.description: the cleaned, truncated (~280 char) leading comment from this variable's own declaration if one exists; failing that, from another declaration of the same name, then from its backing array's own comment, then from a sibling alias into the same backing array; failing all of those, a synthesized fallback stating its type/size and read/write counts
fields.description_source: own | own_other_decl | backing_array | sibling_alias | none -- how confident the description is: 'sibling_alias' means the comment describes the shared backing array/record in general, not necessarily this exact field
fields.rename_suggestion: a human-reviewed candidate g_-prefixed name, populated only for the subset of variables (325 of 1604) whose own declaration or backing array had a real recovery comment to review; null everywhere else, including cases where several DAT_ fields share one record/table comment with no way to tell which specific field is which -- those are left null rather than guessed. This field is a starting point for a future rename pass, not a final answer.

_meta.excluded: 68 DAT_<hex> names that appear only inside comments (historical references to since-renamed/removed symbols), never in live code, are not included here.
